name: THE POIZ RESIDENCES
integration: Integrated with Poiz Centre and Potong Pasir MRT
why_compare: City-fringe reference for the price of direct rail and daily-retail integration
best_fit: Car-lite buyers and families prioritising NEL access over maximum space or freehold tenure
key_risk: Compact-unit mix and leasehold premium face newer integrated competition
future_context: Most Bidadari uplift is realised; remaining polyclinic and Kallang River plans are contextual rather than fresh price evidence

name: PARK PLACE RESIDENCES AT PLQ
integration: Integrated with PLQ and Paya Lebar MRT
why_compare: Closest East-side match to Poiz's mixed-use and direct-rail proposition
best_fit: Buyers wanting dual-line connectivity and a large retail-office hub
key_risk: Larger typical units and a Paya Lebar office-hub premium
future_context: Paya Lebar Air Base redevelopment is strategic context from the 2030s and should not be priced as near-term uplift

name: PARC ESTA
best_fit: Families wanting broad unit choice near Eunos with strong resale depth
key_risk: Mega-project resale competition and a short post-completion history
future_context: Eunos and Paya Lebar regeneration improve long-run context but the project is not directly integrated with MRT or a major mall

name: SEASIDE RESIDENCES
integration: Near Siglap MRT and East Coast Park
why_compare: Measures the East Coast and TEL lifestyle premium
best_fit: Buyers explicitly valuing East Coast Park and coastal living over lowest quantum
key_risk: Sea view and facing create large within-project price dispersion
future_context: Bayshore and TEL investment improve amenities while adding future competing housing supply

name: KATONG REGENCY
integration: Integrated with KINEX near Paya Lebar MRT
best_fit: Buyers who prioritise freehold tenure and mixed-use convenience over transaction depth
key_risk: Thin current bedroom samples and non-comparable freehold tenure
future_context: Paya Lebar transformation is supportive but long-dated; current samples are too thin for a primary numerical control

name: BEDOK RESIDENCES
integration: Integrated with Bedok Mall and Bedok transport hub
why_compare: Closest mature-town integrated comparison to Poiz
best_fit: Households wanting mature-town amenities and more family space with direct transport integration
key_risk: Older project with substantially larger typical family units
future_context: New Bedok and Upper Changi housing adds amenities and eventual resale competition; compare quantum together with floor area

name: THE GLADES
why_compare: Separates MRT proximity from full mixed-use integration
best_fit: Buyers seeking lower PSF and rail access near eastern employment nodes
key_risk: SOHO and dual-key layouts add unit-mix heterogeneity
future_context: TEL5 and DTL extension improve East connectivity but are area context rather than project integration

name: GRANDEUR PARK RESIDENCES
integration: Near Tanah Merah MRT with minor on-site retail
why_compare: Close age and 1-2BR quantum control for Poiz
best_fit: Buyers wanting a newer project near Tanah Merah at Poiz-like compact-unit quantum
key_risk: Newer completion and limited retail are not equivalent to integration
future_context: Eastern rail expansion supports access but does not remove the mixed-use gap versus Poiz

name: TREASURE AT TAMPINES
integration: Large residential project outside direct MRT integration
why_compare: Deepest Tampines family and quantum benchmark
best_fit: Price-sensitive families prioritising facilities and achieved-sale depth over direct rail integration
key_risk: Very large project and recent seller cohort increase internal resale competition
future_context: Tampines Regional Centre and CRL are useful area context but the project is not station-integrated
